messages:
sam: FYI i'm starting a long-running effort called 'stripe-migration-safety' to carve runtime tiles and make service ownership explicit. goal: reduce cross-service KV calls and make tenant-level rollbacks easy. quick sync tmrw?

lyn: +1. can you scope the first tile? which responsibilities move vs stay?

diego: i'd start with session lease + tenant metadata + local KV access. keep model serving, billing, telemetry global. main risk = batch shrink and tail latency.

anya: we must ship a compatibility facade. header-based opt-in (X-Stripe-Ver: v1) and a safe fallback to legacy path if tile fails.

sam: rollout plan: facade behind flag -> single-tenant canary -> cohorted rollout (by traffic shape) -> full. auto-rollback on SLO breach.

lyn: acceptance criteria: p95 token-loop delta <=5%, p99 <=3% increase, per-tenant rollback <5m, and no downstream telemetry schema changes.

diego: batching tradeoff: keep batching shim in facade initially to preserve efficiency, later move batching into tiles for isolation.

anya: migration steps: mark tenant migrating, warm new shard, switch header, drain old shard. lease semantics to avoid split-brain.

ops-bot: reminder: create staging slot and dashboards: runtime.tile.hit_rate, runtime.tile.batch_size, runtime.tile.queue_p99. tag deploys with "stripe-migration".

sam: tests: migration chaos (kill shard mid-switch), semantic diff on canonical prompts, batch-size regression checks. i'll draft RFC + runbook and link here.

lyn: i'll draft the runbook items and rollback knobs; diego can prototype a microbench for warm/migrate.

diego: will drop perf numbers after a small spike test.

ops-bot: note: set canary auto-fail if error rate >1% or p95 regresses >5%.

sam: thanks all. sync tmrw 11:00 PT; i'll post RFC link afterwards.
